core_obligations: Expand an element of the left hand side into its bidegree components and write each component as a finite sum of tensor products of families of maps (proof lines 17980-18000).
Define the image componentwise by composing the two families and summing over the intermediate index (proof lines 18000-18015).
Check that the defining sum is finite for each pair of bidegrees, so that the image is an element of the right hand side (proof lines 18015-18025).
Compare signs to verify compatibility with the differentials, using the displayed differential of each side (proof lines 18025-18032).
proof_roadmap: Define the map by composition (proof lines 18000-18015).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the canonical composition map from the total tensor product of two internal Hom complexes into the internal Hom of the outer two complexes, and the proof is a 54-line argument that gives both the categorical origin of the map and a direct construction. The direct construction expands an element of the left hand side into components indexed by bidegrees and writes each component as a finite sum of tensor products of families of maps, then defines the image componentwise by composing the two families and summing over the intermediate index, and finally checks that the sum is finite and that the result is compatible with the differentials. The finiteness of the sum over the middle index and the sign comparison are the two places where the work lies, and both are displayed.
